Per line: N = normalized Akkadian reconstruction (| metrical foot, || caesura); T = eBL English translation; L = lemmas with eBL dictionary glosses; then notes, parallel lines, and the manuscripts' transliterations (ATF). Bibliography keys like [RN117: 889] are resolved in bibliography.md (RN117 = George 2003).

1'

  • N: [ ... ] (|) rīmī (||) tišānu (|) [ ... ] ...
  • T: […] wild bulls, the aurochs of […,]
  • L: rīmī ← rīmu I “wild bull hunted”; tišānu ← tišānu I “f. tišānītum (a wild animal) OB”
  • Parallels: cf. L I.4 SB "X" 259; cf. L I.4 SB "X" 260; cf. L I.4 SB "X" 261
SipOB1 i 1'. [x x x] ri#-mi ti-ša#-nu# [x x] x x x

2'

  • N: [iltab]aš | maškīšunu || ikkal | šīram
  • T: [he] clothed himself in their skins, eating their flesh.
  • L: [iltab]aš ← labāšu I “to clothe o.s.”; maškīšunu ← mašku I “skin of human”; ikkal ← akālu I “to eat”; šīram ← šīru I “often pl. flesh”
  • Parallels: cf. L I.4 SB "X" 261
SipOB1 i 2'. [il-ta-b]a-aš ma-aš-ki-šu-nu i-ik-ka-al ši-ra-am

3'

  • N: [uharr]i? | būrātim (|) gilgāmeš (||) ša lā ibšiā | matīma
  • T: Gilgameš [dug] wells that never existed before,
  • L: [uharr]i? ← herû II “to dig”; būrātim ← būrtu I “cistern, well”; gilgāmeš ← Gilgameš I; ša ← ša I “who(m), which”; lā ← lā I “not, no”; ibšiā ← bašû I “to be (at hand, available)”; matīma ← matīma I “ever”
SipOB1 i 3'. [u₂?-har?-r]i? bu-ra-tim {d}GIŠ ša la ib-ši-a ma-ti-i-ma

4'

  • N: [iš]tī-ma | mê || iredde | šārī
  • T: [he] drank the water as he chased the winds.
  • L: [iš]tī-ma ← šatû II “to drink”; mê ← mû I “pl. tant. water mê kabrūtim mass of water”; iredde ← redû I “to accompany, lead, drive, proceed”; šārī ← šāru I “pl. also f. wind”
SipOB1 i 4'. [iš?]-ti-i-ma me-e i-re-ed-de ša-ri

5'

  • N: šamšu | ītašuš | idakkussu
  • T: Šamaš became worried, so he bent down to him,
  • L: šamšu ← šamšu I “OB occas. f. sun”; ītašuš ← ašāšu III “to be distressed OA, O/jB”; idakkussu ← dakāšu I “~ to press in O/jB”
SipOB1 i 5'. {d}UTU{+šu} i-ta-šu-uš i-da-ak-ku-us₂-su

6'

  • N: issaqqaram | ana gilgāmeš
  • T: he spoke to Gilgameš:
  • L: issaqqaram ← zakāru I “to speak, say”; ana ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; gilgāmeš ← Gilgameš I
SipOB1 i 6'. is-sa₃-qar-am a-na {d}GIŠ

7'

  • N: gilgāmeš | êš | tadâl
  • T: ‘O Gilgameš, where are you wandering?
  • L: gilgāmeš ← Gilgameš I; êš ← êš I “whither? OB”; tadâl ← dâlu I “to move, roam around O/jB, NA”
  • Parallels: L I.4 OB "VA+BM" a+16
SipOB1 i 7'. {d}GIŠ e-eš ta-da-al

8'

  • N: balāṭam | ša tasahhuru | lā tutta
  • T: You cannot find the life that you seek.’
  • L: balāṭam ← balāṭu I “life esp. ana balāṭ X for X's life”; ša ← ša I “who(m), which”; tasahhuru ← sahāru I “to go around, turn”; lā ← lā I “not, no”; tutta ← watû I “to find, discover”
  • Parallels: L I.4 OB "VA+BM" a+17
SipOB1 i 8'. ba-la-ṭam₂ ša ta-sa-ah-hu-ru la tu-ut-ta

9'

  • N: gilgāmeš | ana šâšum | issaqqar || ana qurādim | šamši
  • T: Gilgameš spoke to him, to the hero Šamaš:
  • L: gilgāmeš ← Gilgameš I; ana ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; šâšum ← šâšu I “(to/of) him Bab., NA”; issaqqar ← zakāru I “to speak, say”; ana ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; qurādim ← qurādu I “hero, warrior of god, king, soldiers”; šamši ← šamšu I “OB occas. f. sun”
SipOB1 i 9'. {d}GIŠ a-na ša-a-šum is-sa₃-qar a-na qu₂-ra-di-im {d}UTU{+ši}

10'

  • N: ištu | eli ṣērim || atalluki | dâlim
  • T: ‘After roaming, wandering through the wild,
  • L: ištu ← ištu I “from, out of”; eli ← eli I “on, over, above”; ṣērim ← ṣēru I “back, upperside”; atalluki ← alāku I “to go”; dâlim ← dâlu I “to move, roam around O/jB, NA”
SipOB1 i 10'. iš-tu e-li ṣe-ri-im a-ta-al-lu-ki da-li-im

11'

  • N: ina libbu | erṣetim || sakāpum | mādū
  • T: within the Netherworld will rest be scarce?
  • L: ina ← ina I “(im-m..., ip-p... etc.) in, on”; libbu ← libbu I “inner body”; erṣetim ← erṣetu I “earth, land”; sakāpum ← sakāpu II “to rest, lie down Bab.”; mādū ← mâdu I “to be(come) many, numerous”
  • Note: The reading mādū follows [RN602: 409].
SipOB1 i 11'. i-na li-ib-bu er-ṣe-tim sa-ka-pu-um ma-du-u₂

12'

  • N: attillam-ma | kalu (|) šanātim
  • T: I shall be lying down down all the years,
  • L: attillam-ma ← itūlu I “to lie down”; kalu ← kalû II “all, totality”; šanātim ← šattu I “f., occas. m.”
SipOB1 i 12'. at-ti-il-lam-ma ka-lu ša-na-tim

13'

  • N: īnāya | šamšam | liṭṭulā-ma || nawirtam | lušbi
  • T: but now let my eyes look on the sun so I am sated with light.
  • L: īnāya ← īnu I “f. eye”; šamšam ← šamšu I “OB occas. f. sun”; liṭṭulā-ma ← naṭālu I “to look”; nawirtam ← nawirtu I “brightness, light O/jB n. šakānu to bring about brightness”; lušbi ← šebû I “to be full (of = acc.)”
SipOB1 i 13'. i#-na-ia ša-am-ša-am! li-iṭ!(IB)-ṭu₂-la-a-ma na-wi-ir-tam lu-uš-bi

14'

  • N: rēqet | ekletum || kī maṣi | nawirtum
  • T: The darkness is hidden, how much light is there?
  • L: rēqet ← rêqu I “to be distant, go far off OAkk, Bab.”; ekletum ← ekletu I “(or iklētu(m)) darkness Bab.”; kī ← kī I “like”; maṣi ← maṣû I “to correspond, comply with (s.th.)”; nawirtum ← nawirtu I “brightness, light O/jB n. šakānu to bring about brightness”
  • Note: For rēqet instead of reqêt < raqû (George), see [RN602: 409].
SipOB1 i 14'. re-qe₂#-e#-et ek-le-tum ki ma-ṣi na-wi-ir-tum

15'

  • N: mat[īma] | mītum || līmuram | šarūru (|) šamši
  • T: When may a dead man see the rays of the sun?
  • L: mat[īma] ← matīma I “ever”; mītum ← mītu I “dead transf. of the (politically) powerless, of city or country”; līmuram ← amāru I “to see”; šarūru ← šarūru I; šamši ← šamšu I “OB occas. f. sun”
SipOB1 i 15'. ma-ti#-[ma] mi-tum# li-mu-ra-am ša-ru-ru {d}UTU{+ši}

a+1

  • N: [ibrī | ša arammûšu | danniš]
  • T: ‘[My friend, whom I love deeply,]
  • L: [ibrī ← ibru I “friend, colleague”; ša ← ša I “who(m), which”; arammûšu ← râmu I “love Bab., NA of deity, person for king, brother, woman”; danniš] ← danniš I “very”
  • Parallels: L I.4 SB "X" 55
SipOB1 ii 0'. [x x x x x x x x x x x x]

a+2

  • N: ittīya | ittallaku (||) kalu (|) marṣātim
  • T: who with me went through every danger,
  • L: ittīya ← itti I “with”; ittallaku ← alāku I “to go”; kalu ← kalû II “all, totality”; marṣātim ← maruṣtu I “evil, distress m. amāru to experience trouble”
  • Parallels: L I.4 SB "X" 55
SipOB1 ii 1'. it#-ti#-ia# it#-ta-al-la-ku ka-lu mar-ṣ[a-a-tim]

a+3

  • N: enkīdu | ša arammûšu | danniš
  • T: Enkidu, whom I love deeply,
  • L: enkīdu ← Enkidu I; ša ← ša I “who(m), which”; arammûšu ← râmu I “love Bab., NA of deity, person for king, brother, woman”; danniš ← danniš I “very”
  • Parallels: L I.4 SB "X" 56
SipOB1 ii 2'. en-ki-du₁₀ ša a-ra-am-mu-šu da-an-ni-iš

a+4

  • N: ittīya | ittallaku (||) kalu (|) marṣātim
  • T: who with me went through every danger:
  • L: ittīya ← itti I “with”; ittallaku ← alāku I “to go”; kalu ← kalû II “all, totality”; marṣātim ← maruṣtu I “evil, distress m. amāru to experience trouble”
  • Parallels: L I.4 SB "X" 56
SipOB1 ii 3'. it-ti-ia it-ta-al-la-ku ka-lu mar-ṣa-a-tim#

a+5

  • N: illik-ma | ana šīmatu (|) awīlūtim
  • T: he went to the destiny of mankind,
  • L: illik-ma ← alāku I “to go”; ana ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; šīmatu ← šīmtu I “st. constr. šīmti, occas. šimit what is fixed”; awīlūtim ← awīlūtu I “humanity”
  • Parallels: L I.4 SB "X" 57
SipOB1 ii 4'. il-li-ik-ma a-na ši-ma-tu a-wi-lu-tim

a+6

  • N: urrī | u mūšī || elīšu | abki
  • T: I wept over him day and night.
  • L: urrī ← urru I “daytime OAkk, Bab., NA”; u ← u I “and, but, also”; mūšī ← mūšu I “night”; elīšu ← eli I “on, over, above”; abki ← bakû I “to weep”
  • Parallels: L I.4 SB "X" 58
SipOB1 ii 5'. ur-ri u₃ mu-ši e-li-šu ab-ki

a+7

  • N: ul addiššu | ana qebērim
  • T: I did not give him up for burial —
  • L: ul ← ul I “not Bab., to negate main clause”; addiššu ← nadānu II “to give”; ana ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; qebērim ← qebēru I “to bury Bab., M/NA”
  • Parallels: L I.4 SB "X" 59
SipOB1 ii 6'. u₂-ul ad-di-iš-šu a-na qe₂-be₂-ri-im

a+8

  • N: ibrī-man | itabbiam | ana rigmīya
  • T: “Maybe my friend will rise at my cry!” —
  • L: ibrī-man ← ibru I, -man I “friend, colleague”; itabbiam ← tebû I “OAkk, Ass. tabā'u(m), NB tabû to get up, arise, set out”; ana ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; rigmīya ← rigmu I “pl. f. voice, cry, noise voice of deity, human”
SipOB1 ii 7'. ib-ri-ma-an i-ta-ab-bi-a-am a-na ri-ig-mi-ia

a+9

  • N: sebet | ūmim || u sebe | mušiātim
  • T: for seven days and seven nights,
  • L: sebet ← sebe I “f. sebet(tu) seven, sebet ūmim sebe mušiātim seven days (and)…”; ūmim ← ūmu I “pl. m. & f. day”; u ← u I “and, but, also”; sebe ← sebe I “f. sebet(tu) seven, sebet ūmim sebe mušiātim seven days (and)…”; mušiātim ← mušītu I “pl. mušiātu, mušâtu night(-time)”
  • Parallels: L I.4 SB "X" 60
SipOB1 ii 8'. se-be₂-et u₄-mi-im u₃ se-be₂ mu-ši-a-tim

a+10

  • N: adi tûltum | imqutam | ina appīšu
  • T: until a maggot dropped from his nostril.
  • L: adi ← adi I “until, as far as”; tûltum ← tûltu I “worm O/jB, NA”; imqutam ← maqātu I “to fall”; ina ← ina I “(im-m..., ip-p... etc.) in, on”; appīšu ← appu I “f. nose Bab., M/NA”
  • Parallels: L I.4 SB "X" 60
SipOB1 ii 9'. a-di tu-ul-tum im-qu₂-tam i-na ap-pi₂-šu

a+11

  • N: ištu warkīšu | ul ūta | balāṭam
  • T: After he was gone I did not find life,
  • L: ištu ← ištu I “from, out of”; warkīšu ← arkû I “(NB cf. uškû I) rear, later”; ul ← ul I “not Bab., to negate main clause”; ūta ← watû I “to find, discover”; balāṭam ← balāṭu I “life esp. ana balāṭ X for X's life”
SipOB1 ii 10'. iš-tu wa-ar-ki-šu u₂-ul u₂-ta ba-la-ṭam₂

a+12

  • N: attanaggiš | kīma hābilim || qabaltu | ṣēri
  • T: as I wandered like a trapper through the midst of the wild.
  • L: attanaggiš ← nagāšu I “to go to(wards) O/jB”; kīma ← kīma I “like”; hābilim ← hābilu I “criminal, wrongdoer O/jB”; qabaltu ← qabaltu I “middle Bab., NA spatially, qablat/qabalti/qabsi āli city centre”; ṣēri ← ṣēru I “back, upperside”
  • Parallels: cf. L I.4 SB "X" 5
SipOB1 ii 11'. at-ta-na-ag-gi-iš ki-ma ha-bi-lim qa₂-ba-al-tu ṣe-ri

a+13

  • N: inanna | sābītum || ātamar | pānīki
  • T: Now, ale-wife, I have seen your face,
  • L: inanna ← inanna I “now OAkk, Bab. absol., and after prep., adi i. till now, kīma i.…”; sābītum ← sābītu I “female brewer, alehouse keeper O/jB”; ātamar ← amāru I “to see”; pānīki ← pānu I “front, pl. face”
SipOB1 ii 12'. i-na-an-na sa-bi-tum a-ta-mar pa-ni-ki

a+14

  • N: mūtam | ša ātanaddaru | ai āmur
  • T: but I would not see death, that ever I fear.’
  • L: mūtam ← mūtu I “death”; ša ← ša I “who(m), which”; ātanaddaru ← adāru II “to be afraid (of), fear”; ai ← ai I “(before consonant), â, ya not”; āmur ← amāru I “to see”
SipOB1 ii 13'. mu-tam ša a-ta-na-ad-da-ru a-ia a-mu-ur

a+15

  • N: sābītum | ana šâšum || issaqqaram | ana gilgāmeš
  • T: The ale-wife spoke to him, to Gilgameš:
  • L: sābītum ← sābītu I “female brewer, alehouse keeper O/jB”; ana ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; šâšum ← šâšu I “(to/of) him Bab., NA”; issaqqaram ← zakāru I “to speak, say”; ana ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; gilgāmeš ← Gilgameš I
SipOB1 ii 14'. sa-bi-tum a-na ša-a-šum is-sa₃-qar-am a-na {d}GIŠ

a+16

  • N: gilgāmeš | êš | tadâl
  • T: ‘O Gilgameš, where are you wandering?
  • L: gilgāmeš ← Gilgameš I; êš ← êš I “whither? OB”; tadâl ← dâlu I “to move, roam around O/jB, NA”
  • Parallels: L I.4 OB "VA+BM" 7'
SipOB1 iii 1. {d}GIŠ e-eš ta-da-a-al

a+17

  • N: balāṭam | ša tasahhuru | lā tutta
  • T: You cannot find the life that you seek:
  • L: balāṭam ← balāṭu I “life esp. ana balāṭ X for X's life”; ša ← ša I “who(m), which”; tasahhuru ← sahāru I “to go around, turn”; lā ← lā I “not, no”; tutta ← watû I “to find, discover”
  • Parallels: L I.4 OB "VA+BM" 8'
SipOB1 iii 2. ba-la-ṭam₂ ša ta-sa-ah-hu-ru la tu-ut-ta

a+18

  • N: inūma | ilū || ibnû | awīlūtam
  • T: when the gods created mankind,
  • L: inūma ← inūma I “when Bab.”; ilū ← ilu I “pl. ilū, ilānu god, deity a or the god, also du.”; ibnû ← banû IV “to create”; awīlūtam ← awīlūtu I “humanity”
SipOB1 iii 3. i-nu-ma DINGIR-MEŠ ib-nu-u₂ a-wi-lu-tam

a+19

  • N: mūtam | iškunū | ana awīlūtim
  • T: for mankind they established death,
  • L: mūtam ← mūtu I “death”; iškunū ← šakānu I “to put, place, lay down”; ana ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; awīlūtim ← awīlūtu I “humanity”
SipOB1 iii 4. mu-tam iš-ku-nu a-na a-wi-lu-tim

a+20

  • N: balāṭam | ina qātīšunu | iṣṣabtū
  • T: life they kept for themselves.
  • L: balāṭam ← balāṭu I “life esp. ana balāṭ X for X's life”; ina ← ina I “(im-m..., ip-p... etc.) in, on”; qātīšunu ← qātu I “f.”; iṣṣabtū ← ṣabātu I “to seize, take”
SipOB1 iii 5. ba-la-ṭam₂ i-na qa₂-ti-šu-nu iṣ-ṣa-ab-tu

a+21

  • N: attā | gilgāmeš || lū mali | karaška
  • T: You, Gilgameš, let your belly be full,
  • L: attā ← attā I “you (2 m. sg. pron.)”; gilgāmeš ← Gilgameš I; lū ← lū I “let it be”; mali ← malû IV “to be(come) full”; karaška ← karšu I “m. & f. stomach, interior”
